scope: One diagnostic 1:1 print + one MODE ring only. No five-ring stack, sensing, load-bearing use or electronics.

before.observed: Exact print template and build notes exist; no physical ring geometry/detent has been validated in this receipt.
before.question: Does the printed strip produce a freely rotating, legible 4-position ring with a usable simple detent around the intended ~50 mm core?

use: Print exactly one template sheet at 100% / Actual Size / no fit-to-page.
Measure the MODE strip before cutting: active circumference 163.4 mm plus 10 mm glue tab; ring height 22 mm.
Cut only the MODE strip and its four top V-notches.
Pre-curve and glue around a ~50 mm OD sacrificial tube/core; ring must rotate freely.
Add one temporary fixed reference spine 1–2 mm above the ring.
Add one light paperclip-tip or card-spring detent.
Cycle AIR → LIGHT → CLEAN → FEED → AIR four times; pick up the specimen once and check whether detent holds.

after.required_state: One physical MODE-ring specimen and a PASS/FAIL decision for print scale, circumference, rotation clearance, centering/readability and detent hold.

evidence: Photo of uncut printed MODE strip with ruler showing active 163.4 mm region + 10 mm tab and 22 mm height.
Photo of assembled ring centered on AIR under the reference spine.
Four-position mini-log: token, centers cleanly Y/N, rotates freely Y/N, detent holds Y/N.
pass_gate: Printed dimensions are within practical cutting tolerance of the declared template.
All four positions are individually readable and center under the same reference.
Detent holds position during ordinary pickup but can be intentionally advanced.
next: If PASS, build the remaining four rings and run the documented 20-command Experiment A. If FAIL, change exactly one defect class—print scale, circumference/core fit, notch/detent geometry, or reference-spine clearance—and rerun one ring.
